analysis: The code snippet defines a static method execute(Runnable command) that delegates to UserThread.executor.execute(command). The documentation of the called execute method indicates it can throw NullPointerException if command is null, and RejectedExecutionException if the executor cannot accept the task. In the snippet, there is no null check on command, no try-catch block, and no validation of the executor's state. Therefore, both exceptions can be thrown and are not avoided in the calling context.
answer: NullPointerException: not avoided because there is no null check before passing command to executor.execute(). RejectedExecutionException: not avoided because there is no handling for rejection from the executor.
remark: NullPointerException occurs if the caller passes a null argument to the execute method. RejectedExecutionException occurs if the underlying executor (UserThread.executor) cannot accept the task, e.g., if it is shut down or has reached capacity limits.
